# camt.053 výpis banky do Excelu: prevod bankového výpisu na tabuľku

Language versions: Slovak https://arling.sk/camt053-to-excel/ · English https://arling.sk/camt053-to-excel/en/ · German https://arling.sk/camt053-to-excel/de/

**English summary:** a free, client-side tool that turns a camt.053 XML bank statement (ISO 20022) into a plain CSV/Excel table, entirely in the browser. Beyond Tatra banka/SLSP/VÚB/ČSOB in Slovakia, camt.053 is the standard electronic statement format at any bank in Germany, Austria and Switzerland (Sparkasse, Volksbank, Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank, Raiffeisen, Erste, UBS, PostFinance, and others), so the page itself now ships in Slovak, English and German: a language switcher in the header (also reachable via `?lang=sk|en|de`) translates the hero, playground labels, column headers, FAQ, and Pro section, and switches the CSV export defaults (decimal comma + semicolon for SK/DE, decimal point + comma for EN; date format dd.mm.yyyy for SK/DE, yyyy-mm-dd for EN) and the accounting-software CSV presets (DATEV/Lexware/sevDesk generic layouts, offered for DE/EN).

> Free, client-side tool that turns a camt.053 XML bank statement (výpis z účtu, ISO 20022) from Tatra banka, Slovenská sporiteľňa (SLSP), VÚB, ČSOB, or any German, Austrian or Swiss bank into a plain CSV/Excel table.

No account, no backend, no upload of your statement data: everything from reading the XML to building the table runs in your browser.

## Why this exists

Every one of the four major Slovak banks issues its accounting
statement (výpis do účtovníctva) as camt.053 XML by default: it's the
"SEPA XML SK štandard" the Slovak Bank Association (SBA) published in
2013, based on the ISO 20022 camt.053 schema. That's a good format for
accounting software with a built-in importer, but plenty of real
workflows don't have one wired up: a bookkeeper reconciling payments
against invoices by variabilný symbol, a director doing a manual spot
check on what actually posted this month, a small business whose
software imports CSV but not camt.053 directly. All of these need the
statement as a table, not as XML, and the direct route (open the file
by hand, or buy software that imports it) is more friction than the
problem deserves. This tool is the shortcut: upload the file, download
the table.

## Input format

### 1. The statement file(s)

Upload one or more `.xml` files with the file picker, or paste the XML
text directly into the page. An uploaded file is read with the
browser's own `FileReader` API; it is never sent anywhere. Multiple
files can be converted in the same sitting (several months of
statements, or several accounts), each producing its own table and its
own CSV download.

### 2. Supported camt.053 versions

| Version | Namespace | Where it's used |
|---|---|---|
| camt.053.001.02 | `urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:camt.053.001.02` | The version behind the SBA's 2013 "SEPA XML SK štandard": what Tatra banka, Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, and ČSOB all generate when you choose "výpis do účtovníctva" / "XML - camt.053 SK štandard" in internet banking. |
| camt.053.001.08 | `urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:camt.053.001.08` | A newer ISO 20022 revision. Not what the four Slovak banks above issue today, but accepted for a statement from a non-Slovak bank, a different account-servicing system, or a source that has moved to the newer schema. |

Both versions carry the same core `Ntry` (entry) fields this tool
reads: `BookgDt`, `ValDt`, `Amt`, `CdtDbtInd`, and the remittance/
reference and counterparty-party fields. A file in a different
namespace (camt.052, camt.054, an unrelated XML file) is rejected with
a message naming the namespace found, instead of silently producing an
empty or wrong table.

## What gets read out of the XML

One row per underlying payment. A plain `<Ntry>` with no `NtryDtls/TxDtls`
becomes one row; an `<Ntry>` batching several `TxDtls` blocks (a bulk
credit, for instance) becomes one row per `TxDtls`, each with its own
amount and direction where the transaction detail carries one, falling
back to the entry-level amount otherwise. That way VS/ŠS/KS pairing
against invoices works per payment, not per bank-side batch line.

| Column | Source in the XML | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Číslo výpisu | `Stmt/Id` | Identifies which uploaded statement a row came from, once several files are converted together. |
| Účet (IBAN) | `Stmt/Acct/Id/IBAN` | The statement's own account, not the counterparty. |
| Dátum zaúčtovania | `BookgDt/Dt` (or `DtTm`) | The date the entry posted to the account ledger. |
| Dátum valuty | `ValDt/Dt` (or `DtTm`) | The value date used for interest calculation; can differ from the booking date. |
| Suma | `Amt`, signed by `CdtDbtInd` | `CdtDbtInd = DBIT` makes the row's amount negative; `CRDT` keeps it positive, so a plain SUM() over the column gives the net change to the account. |
| Mena | `Amt/@Ccy`, falling back to the account's own currency | The `Ccy` attribute on the `Amt` element. |
| Status | `Sts` (e.g. `BOOK`, `PDNG`) | Whether the entry is booked or still pending, when the statement distinguishes them. |
| Referencia banky | `AcctSvcrRef`, falling back to `NtryRef` | The bank's own reference for the entry, useful for matching a row back to what's shown in internet banking. |
| Typ transakcie | `BkTxCd`: `Domn/Cd`-`Fmly/Cd`-`Fmly/SubFmlyCd` and/or the bank's own `Prtry/Cd` | e.g. `PMNT-RCDT-ESCT` for an incoming SEPA credit transfer; shown alongside a bank-proprietary code like `PMNT-RCDT (TATRA)` when the statement carries one. |
| Protistrana | `RltdPties/Dbtr` or `/Cdtr` | Name of the other side of the transaction: the creditor's name on a debit entry, the debtor's name on a credit entry (confirmed against a real Tatra banka sample: a DBIT entry carries `Cdtr`, not `Dbtr`). |
| IBAN protistrany | `RltdPties/DbtrAcct` or `/CdtrAcct` | The counterparty's IBAN, when the statement carries it (not every entry does; bank-fee and utility-style lines in particular often don't). |
| BIC protistrany | `RltdAgts/DbtrAgt` or `/CdtrAgt` (`FinInstnId/BIC` or `/BICFI`) | The counterparty's bank, where present. |
| EndToEndId | `Refs/EndToEndId` | The end-to-end reference as the bank recorded it, VS/ŠS/KS packing included. |
| VS / ŠS / KS | Parsed from `EndToEndId`'s `/VS.../SS.../KS...` convention, the structured remittance reference, or, failing both, pattern-matched out of the free-text message | The same National Bank of Slovakia convention the sibling SEPA pain.001 tools already document and check, so a statement generated from a pain.001 file built by SEPA pain.001 Generátor round-trips its VS/ŠS/KS back out. |
| Správa pre príjemcu | `RmtInf/Ustrd` (all instances joined) | Free-text remittance info. |
| Poplatok | `Chrgs/TtlChrgsAndTaxAmt`, falling back to `Chrgs/Amt` | Any fee the entry itself carries, separate from its main amount. |

The statement header (`Stmt/Acct`, `Stmt/Bal`, `Stmt/Svcr`) is also
read, for a summary above the table: account IBAN, statement period
(`FrToDt`), entry/credit/debit counts and totals, and opening/closing
balance (`Bal` entries with codes `OPBD`/`PRCD` and `CLBD`/`CLAV`).
Opening balance plus the net of every entry is checked against the
reported closing balance, so a mismatch is visible before the
row-level data is trusted. The servicing bank's BIC (`Svcr/FinInstnId/
BIC`) is matched against Tatra banka, SLSP, VÚB, ČSOB, and eight other
Slovak banks' BICs to label which bank issued the file.

## Worked example

This is the Slovak sample statement the tool ships (the "ukážka" button
loads exactly this XML when the page is in Slovak), a camt.053.001.02
statement with three entries: one incoming SEPA credit transfer, one
outgoing payment, and one service fee. When the page is in German or
English, the same button loads a German bank statement instead: a
camt.053.001.02 export for a fictional Muster GmbH at a fictional
Musterbank (BIC MUSTDEFFXXX) with four entries (a received
SEPA-Überweisung with Rechnungsnummer and Kundenreferenz, a paid
SEPA-Lastschrift with mandate reference and Gläubiger-ID, a girocard
card payment, and a bank fee), exported as `SAMPLE_CAMT053_XML_DE` from
`camt053.js`.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:camt.053.001.02">
  <BkToCstmrStmt>
    <GrpHdr>
      <MsgId>ARL-20260906-000001</MsgId>
      <CreDtTm>2026-09-06T08:00:00+02:00</CreDtTm>
    </GrpHdr>
    <Stmt>
      <Id>SK6809000000000012345678-001-260906</Id>
      <FrToDt>
        <FrDtTm>2026-09-01T00:00:00+02:00</FrDtTm>
        <ToDtTm>2026-09-05T23:59:59+02:00</ToDtTm>
      </FrToDt>
      <Acct>
        <Id><IBAN>SK6809000000000012345678</IBAN></Id>
        <Ccy>EUR</Ccy>
        <Ownr><Nm>Ukazkova firma s. r. o.</Nm></Ownr>
      </Acct>
      <Svcr><FinInstnId><BIC>TATRSKBX</BIC></FinInstnId></Svcr>
      <Bal>
        <Tp><CdOrPrtry><Cd>OPBD</Cd></CdOrPrtry></Tp>
        <Amt Ccy="EUR">1000.00</Amt><CdtDbtInd>CRDT</CdtDbtInd>
        <Dt><Dt>2026-09-01</Dt></Dt>
      </Bal>
      <Bal>
        <Tp><CdOrPrtry><Cd>CLBD</Cd></CdOrPrtry></Tp>
        <Amt Ccy="EUR">1239.30</Amt><CdtDbtInd>CRDT</CdtDbtInd>
        <Dt><Dt>2026-09-05</Dt></Dt>
      </Bal>
      <Ntry>
        <NtryRef>2026090100001</NtryRef>
        <Amt Ccy="EUR">450.00</Amt><CdtDbtInd>CRDT</CdtDbtInd><Sts>BOOK</Sts>
        <BookgDt><Dt>2026-09-02</Dt></BookgDt><ValDt><Dt>2026-09-02</Dt></ValDt>
        <NtryDtls><TxDtls>
          <Refs><AcctSvcrRef>2026090100001</AcctSvcrRef><EndToEndId>/VS2026001/SS0000/KS0308</EndToEndId></Refs>
          <BkTxCd><Domn><Cd>PMNT</Cd><Fmly><Cd>RCDT</Cd><SubFmlyCd>ESCT</SubFmlyCd></Fmly></Domn></BkTxCd>
          <RltdPties><Dbtr><Nm>Jozef Odberatel</Nm></Dbtr><DbtrAcct><Id><IBAN>SK0502000000272000000018</IBAN></Id></DbtrAcct></RltdPties>
          <RltdAgts><DbtrAgt><FinInstnId><BIC>SUBASKBX</BIC></FinInstnId></DbtrAgt></RltdAgts>
          <RmtInf><Ustrd>Uhrada faktury 2026-0912</Ustrd></RmtInf>
        </TxDtls></NtryDtls>
      </Ntry>
      <Ntry>
        <NtryRef>2026090300002</NtryRef>
        <Amt Ccy="EUR">89.90</Amt><CdtDbtInd>DBIT</CdtDbtInd><Sts>BOOK</Sts>
        <BookgDt><Dt>2026-09-03</Dt></BookgDt><ValDt><Dt>2026-09-03</Dt></ValDt>
        <NtryDtls><TxDtls>
          <Refs><AcctSvcrRef>2026090300002</AcctSvcrRef><EndToEndId>/VS789/KS0308</EndToEndId></Refs>
          <BkTxCd><Domn><Cd>PMNT</Cd><Fmly><Cd>ICDT</Cd><SubFmlyCd>ESCT</SubFmlyCd></Fmly></Domn></BkTxCd>
          <RltdPties><Cdtr><Nm>Dodavatel Novak s. r. o.</Nm></Cdtr><CdtrAcct><Id><IBAN>SK8709000000002000000018</IBAN></Id></CdtrAcct></RltdPties>
          <RltdAgts><CdtrAgt><FinInstnId><BIC>GIBASKBX</BIC></FinInstnId></CdtrAgt></RltdAgts>
          <RmtInf><Ustrd>Kancelarske potreby</Ustrd></RmtInf>
        </TxDtls></NtryDtls>
      </Ntry>
      <Ntry>
        <NtryRef>2026090500003</NtryRef>
        <Amt Ccy="EUR">120.80</Amt><CdtDbtInd>DBIT</CdtDbtInd><Sts>BOOK</Sts>
        <BookgDt><Dt>2026-09-05</Dt></BookgDt><ValDt><Dt>2026-09-05</Dt></ValDt>
        <NtryDtls><TxDtls>
          <Refs><AcctSvcrRef>2026090500003</AcctSvcrRef><EndToEndId>NOTPROVIDED</EndToEndId></Refs>
          <RltdPties><Cdtr><Nm>Energie SK a. s.</Nm></Cdtr><CdtrAcct><Id><IBAN>SK5809000000000123456789</IBAN></Id></CdtrAcct></RltdPties>
          <RmtInf><Ustrd>Zaloha elektrina VS: 445566</Ustrd></RmtInf>
        </TxDtls></NtryDtls>
      </Ntry>
    </Stmt>
  </BkToCstmrStmt>
</Document>
```

Output table (columns trimmed to the ones with content, for space):

| Dátum zaúčt. | Suma | Protistrana | IBAN protistrany | VS | KS | Správa pre príjemcu |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-02 | 450.00 | Jozef Odberatel | SK0502000000272000000018 | 2026001 | 0308 | Uhrada faktury 2026-0912 |
| 2026-09-03 | -89.90 | Dodavatel Novak s. r. o. | SK8709000000002000000018 | 789 | 0308 | Kancelarske potreby |
| 2026-09-05 | -120.80 | Energie SK a. s. | SK5809000000000123456789 | 445566 (z textu) | | Zaloha elektrina VS: 445566 |

Summary above the table: účet `SK6809000000000012345678`, banka Tatra
banka (BIC `TATRSKBX`), obdobie `2026-09-01` to `2026-09-05`,
počiatočný zostatok `1000.00 EUR`, konečný zostatok `1239.30 EUR`.
`1000.00 + 450.00 - 89.90 - 120.80 = 1239.30`: the three rows account
for the whole balance change, so the built-in check passes. The third
entry has no `EndToEndId` (its bank sent `NOTPROVIDED`), so its VS is
instead picked up from the free-text message "Zaloha elektrina VS:
445566", the same fallback a human reading the statement would use.

## How it works

Static HTML plus one dependency-free JavaScript engine, `camt053.js`,
loaded as an ES module and also publishing `window.CamtConverter =
{parse, toRows, toCsv, summarize}` for console/debug use. In the
browser it parses the XML with the native `DOMParser`; the same file
also runs unmodified under Node (used by this project's own
`tests.mjs` test suite) via a small dependency-free tolerant XML
parser, the same approach this project's sibling tool, SEPA pain.001
Doctor, uses for its own XML parsing, so the exact same code path is
exercised in both environments instead of two parallel implementations
that could drift apart. There is no backend, no upload, and no request
that carries your statement data anywhere: read `index.html` and
`camt053.js` directly to verify.

## Who it's for

Accountants, bookkeepers, and company directors in Slovakia, Germany,
Austria and Switzerland who download a camt.053 statement from
internet banking (Tatra banka, SLSP, VÚB, ČSOB, or any DE/AT/CH bank)
and need the transactions as a table: reconciling payments against
invoices (by variabilný symbol in Slovakia, or the Verwendungszweck/
remittance text elsewhere), a manual check on what actually posted, or
a bookkeeping process that has no direct camt.053 importer of its own.

## FAQ

**Why does it ask for a camt.053 version, or mention .001.02 vs
.001.08?**
It doesn't ask; it detects the version from the `xmlns` on the
statement's `<Document>` element and reads either. `.001.02` is what
Tatra banka, SLSP, VÚB, and ČSOB all issue today (the SBA's SEPA XML
SK štandard); `.001.08` is supported in case the statement comes from
elsewhere. Both use the same entry-level fields this tool reads, so
the output looks the same either way.

**My bank isn't Tatra banka, SLSP, VÚB, or ČSOB. Will it still work?**
If the file is valid camt.053.001.02 or .001.08 XML, yes: the parser
reads the standard ISO 20022 entry fields, not anything specific to
one of the four banks. Those four are simply the ones confirmed to
issue exactly this format for a Slovak account.

**Does it check that the statement is correct, or that the balances
add up?**
It reads and displays the opening/closing balance the statement itself
reports, so you can compare it against the sum of the converted rows
by eye, but it doesn't reject a file whose entries don't sum to the
stated balance: a mismatch usually means an entry type (e.g. a pending
or a reversed transaction) isn't captured the way you expected, worth
checking against the original XML rather than a sign the tool
miscalculated.

**Is there a limit on how many entries or files I can convert?**
Not in this tool. A very large statement (thousands of entries) parses
more slowly since everything runs in your browser's own JavaScript
engine, but there's no artificial cap.

**Can I paste the XML instead of uploading a file?**
Yes. Uploading with the file picker and pasting the XML text both feed
the same parser; use whichever is easier to get the content into the
page.

**What happens if the file isn't a camt.053 statement at all (wrong
namespace, camt.052/camt.054, unrelated XML)?**
The tool reports the namespace it found instead of the one it expects,
rather than producing an empty or silently wrong table.

**Does anything about my statement get uploaded when I use the file
picker?**
No. The file is read locally with the browser's `FileReader` API, the
same as pasted text would be, and never leaves the page.

**Can it convert camt.053 to MT940 for DATEV?**
Yes, as a Pro (licensed) feature: `mt940.js` builds one SWIFT MT940
message per statement, with the German `:86:` structured subfield
convention (GVC code, `?00`-`?34` subfields, SEPA `EREF+`/`SVWZ+` tags),
for a manual import into DATEV Kanzlei-Rechnungswesen or any other
MT940-only software. German banks stopped issuing MT940 in November
2025 (camt.053 only, per the banking industry's own rulebook), but
DATEV's manual file import still expects MT940, since DATEV has no
direct camt.053 file import of its own. `datev-extf.js` additionally
exports straight into the DATEV-Format "Buchungsstapel" (EXTF CSV), with
a small Konto/Sachkontenlänge/Beraternummer/Mandantennummer/
Wirtschaftsjahr-Beginn options block. Both exports run client-side like
the rest of the tool; without a Pro licence, the button shows a preview
of the file's first 8 lines instead of downloading it.

**Is there a developer API, not just the page UI?**
Yes: `camt053.js` is a plain ES module exporting `parse` (XML string to
statement objects), `toRows` (statement objects to the row table
described above), `toCsv` (rows to a CSV string), and `summarize`
(account/period/balance header). It has no dependency, so it can be
imported into another Node or browser project directly instead of
scraping the page.

## Privacy

No account, no login, no cookies for the tool itself, no server-side
processing of your statement. The only analytics are anonymous usage
counts (event name + count, never IBANs, names, or amounts) sent to a
self-hosted Umami instance. The only exception is the optional
mailing-list form: if you type an email address into it, that address
is sent to the subscribe endpoint and nothing else.
